name: Methyldiazinol

angle.text: A 1965 laboratory curiosity with a high reported animal muscle-to-androgen ratio, which is the basis of any interest in it for muscle building. It was never marketed and nothing else is on record.

summary: A 1965 lab-curiosity DHT steroid with a high reported animal muscle-to-androgen ratio and nothing else on record.
note: Never marketed; no human data and no verifiable modern supplement documentation.
currentQuick:
Methyldiazinol is an obscure oral steroid synthesised in the 1960s as a modified version of mestanolone. It was never sold as a drug.
The only reported pharmacology is an old animal measurement suggesting a high muscle-to-androgenic ratio.
How it works: It is a 17α-methylated DHT analogue with a diazirine group at carbon 3; its mechanism has not been described beyond presumed androgen activity.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data exist and it has no approved use.
deepLead:
Methyldiazinol (3,3-azo-17α-methyl-5α-dihydrotestosterone, or 3-azi-17α-methyl-DHT) is a synthetic, orally active androgen and anabolic steroid that was never marketed . It is a 17α-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone, specifically the 3-azi (diazirine) analogue of mestanolone .
It is described in a 1965 paper by Church, Kende and Weiss on the preparation of steroid diaziridines and diazirines . Wikipedia reports a muscle-building to androgenic ratio of 15 relative to oral methyltestosterone, among the highest recorded in the old animal literature .
Only that early animal-era data and chemistry exist; no human studies have been published.

name: Epistane (Epitiostanol-derivative, Havoc)

angle.text: Sold online as a supplement since about 2009, it is used by lifters who want a harder, leaner muscular look. Nobody has trialled it, and case reports link it to liver bile-flow problems.

summary: An oral designer steroid once sold as a supplement; case reports link it to liver bile-flow problems and nobody has trialled it.
note: Controlled steroid in the US since 2014; prohibited in sport; cholestasis case reports.
currentQuick:
Epistane is an oral anabolic steroid related to epitiostanol, a Japanese breast-cancer drug. It was never approved, but began appearing in online muscle supplements around 2009.
No clinical trials have tested it for muscle or appearance. What exists in the literature is chemical analysis of products and a small set of case reports.
How it works: It is a 17alpha-methylated androgen from the DHT family. Laboratory work on human liver cells suggests it increases bile acid synthesis and interacts with nuclear receptors.
Risks and caveats: A 2020 case series reported prolonged cholestasis in four users. Its 17alpha-methyl group is associated with liver toxicity. It is a controlled steroid in the US since 2014 and is prohibited by WADA.
deepLead:
Epistane, also called methylepitiostanol, 17alpha-methylepithiostanol, Havoc or Epi Plex, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from epitiostanol, a compound once used in Japan for breast cancer. It was never marketed as a medicine, but it has been sold online as a bodybuilding supplement since about 2009.
Analytical chemists identified it in over-the-counter products around 2009 and reported that the ingredient is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list. In 2014 it was named among the steroids controlled under the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act.
No controlled trials in healthy users have been published. The main human data are case reports: a 2020 toxicology study described four people who developed long-lasting cholestasis after taking it.

name: Methoxydienone (Methoxy / 18-methyl)

angle.text: A nandrolone-family steroid from contraceptive research that surfaced as a designer supplement for muscle building. No human trials exist for that use.

summary: A nandrolone-family designer steroid from contraceptive research that surfaced in supplements; no human trials exist.
note: Never approved; a forensic case shows it can cause positive doping results.
currentQuick:
Methoxydienone is a 19-nortestosterone steroid synthesised in the 1960s and 70s during progestin research. It was never a medicine, and appeared later in online supplements.
No clinical studies have examined it in people.
How it works: It is an anabolic-androgenic steroid and progestogen; animal-derived ratios reported on Wikipedia suggest anabolic activity when injected. Oral activity in humans has not been characterised.
Risks and caveats: No safety data in humans are published. A 2022 case report tied a supplement containing it to a detected 18-methyl steroid metabolite in a forensic urine sample, relevant for drug testing.
deepLead:
Methoxydienone, also called methoxygonadiene, is a synthetic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group, related to the progestin levonorgestrel. It was never marketed as a medicine but has been sold online as a 'designer steroid' supplement ingredient.
It was synthesised by Herchel Smith and colleagues in the 1960s and 1970s during work on oral contraceptive progestins. No human trials of it exist; the published literature on its use in people is a forensic case report.

name: Bolandione

angle.text: A nandrolone prohormone sold over the counter in the US until 2005 for muscle gain. It is now controlled and best known for causing doping-test positives; human evidence for the physique effect is thin.

summary: A nandrolone prohormone from the supplement era; now controlled and best known for causing doping-test positives.
note: US Schedule III; banned in sport.
currentQuick:
Bolandione is a prohormone that the body converts to nandrolone. It was sold as a supplement in the US until 2005.
It is now a controlled substance and is chiefly remembered for doping-test false positives.
How it works: Oral intake leads to conversion to nandrolone; its own androgen receptor activity is weaker than DHT.
Risks and caveats: US Schedule III and prohibited in sport. Animal data suggest oral routes are inefficient for muscle but may still cause side effects, per Wikipedia.
deepLead:
Bolandione, also known as 19-norandrostenedione or estr-4-ene-3,17-dione, is a steroid that acts as a precursor of the anabolic steroid nandrolone. It was sold without prescription in the United States as a prohormone supplement until 2005.
It is a US Schedule III controlled substance and is banned under the World Anti-Doping Code. Trace amounts in androstenedione products produced false-positive nandrolone doping tests in the early 2000s.

name: 19-Nor-4-androstenedione (19-norandrostenedione)

angle.text: Sold as an over-the-counter nandrolone prohormone in the US until 2005, used by bodybuilders for muscle gain. Today it is mostly a doping-control footnote, with little evidence on the physique use.

summary: A nandrolone prohormone from the supplement era, now mostly a doping-control footnote.
note: Controlled in the US; prohibited in sport; can cause positive nandrolone tests.
currentQuick:
19-Norandrostenedione is a prohormone that converts to nandrolone. It was sold as a supplement in the US until 2005.
Research on it centres on doping tests rather than muscle outcomes.
How it works: After oral intake it converts to nandrolone and shares its urinary metabolite.
Risks and caveats: US Schedule III, banned in sport. Contaminated supplements have caused positive nandrolone tests.
deepLead:
19-Nor-4-androstenedione, also called 19-norandrostenedione or bolandione, is a steroid that is a precursor of nandrolone. It was sold over the counter in the US as a prohormone supplement until 2005.
It is best documented in the literature through doping research. A 2000 JAMA study found trace contamination of over-the-counter androstenedione products and examined whether androstenedione and 19-norandrostenedione ingestion causes positive urine tests for a nandrolone metabolite.

name: Trendione

angle.text: A trenbolone metabolite sold online as a prohormone-type supplement for muscle and a harder look. It has been studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental research, not in people.

summary: A trenbolone metabolite sold as a prohormone; studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental research, not in people.
note: Listed in the US 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act.
currentQuick:
Trendione is a trenbolone metabolite that has been sold online as a prohormone supplement. It is listed in the US 2014 designer steroid law.
No human studies exist.
How it works: It is inactive by itself in receptor assays; the idea is that the body converts it to trenbolone.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data. Legal restrictions apply in the US.
deepLead:
Trendione (estra-4,9,11-triene-3,17-dione; code RU-2065; nicknamed 'Trenavar') is a metabolite of the anabolic steroid trenbolone and has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement.
It is inactive itself, with more than 100-fold lower affinity than trenbolone for androgen and progesterone receptors. Most published work on it concerns environmental fate: trenbolone acetate is used as a cattle growth implant, and trendione is excreted in manure. It is listed in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014.

name: Dienedione

angle.text: Marketed as a trenbolone-type prohormone supplement for muscle gain until it was scheduled in 2010. No human studies exist for its muscle effects.

summary: A trenbolone-type prohormone sold as a supplement until it was scheduled in 2010; no human studies exist.
note: US Schedule III since 2010.
currentQuick:
Dienedione is a 19-nortestosterone steroid that was sold as a bodybuilding prohormone. It was scheduled in the US in 2010.
Research is limited to doping control, notably in horses.
How it works: It is thought to act as a prohormone to dienolone, a compound structurally close to trenbolone.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data. Controlled in the US and UK and prohibited in sport.
deepLead:
Dienedione (estra-4,9-diene-3,17-dione) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group that was never medically used. It is thought to be a prohormone of dienolone and was sold as a bodybuilding supplement, often marketed as a trenbolone prohormone.
It became a US Schedule III steroid on January 4, 2010 and is Class C in the UK. The published research is about doping control, particularly in horses.

name: 4-Androstenediol (4-AD)

angle.text: An early-2000s oral prohormone marketed to raise testosterone and support muscle growth. The muscle claims were large, and human evidence for them is limited.

summary: A 2000s-era oral testosterone prohormone supplement; sold on big muscle claims, with little human evidence behind them.
note: Related prohormones are banned in sport; no human appearance trials found.
currentQuick:
4-Androstenediol is a steroid closely related to testosterone that was sold as an oral supplement in the 2000s, with claims it would raise testosterone and build muscle.
No controlled trial of it for physique goals turned up. Reviews of the wider prohormone class describe the marketing claims as poorly supported.
How it works: It is reported to convert to testosterone in the body at a modest rate, partly via a different enzyme pathway than androstenedione, and some of the resulting testosterone can convert to estrogen. In vitro data show testis tissue can make the conversion.
Risks and caveats: Reviews of oral andro prohormones raised concerns about health risks, and related 19-nor prohormones are on the WADA prohibited list. Specific legal status was not documented in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
4-Androstenediol (androst-4-ene-3β,17β-diol, often abbreviated 4-AD or 4-diol) is an androgen-related steroid that was sold in the early 2000s as an oral "prohormone" dietary supplement, marketed to raise testosterone and support muscle growth. It is a close chemical relative of testosterone and is described as converting to testosterone in the body at a low rate.
Laboratory work shows that rat testis tissue can convert 4-androstenediol to testosterone in vitro, and the compound has been studied mainly in the context of doping detection, where urinary markers have been developed to identify its administration in athletes. A review of the broader "andro" prohormone class concluded that marketing claims of increased testosterone, strength and muscle mass had not been well supported by controlled human studies and that potential health risks were a concern.
No clinical trial of 4-androstenediol for appearance or physique goals was found in the sources reviewed.

name: 1-Androsterone (1-Andro)

angle.text: A designer DHEA-type prohormone sold online as a dietary supplement for muscle gain. It is known from seizure and doping-detection papers, with no human trials.

summary: A designer DHEA-type prohormone sold online for muscle; known from seizure and doping-detection papers, with no human trials.
note: Regulators and WADA treat such products as related to anabolic steroids.
currentQuick:
1-Androsterone is an oral designer steroid sold as a supplement for muscle gain. It is a chemical variant of DHEA.
It appears in the literature mainly because a seized product was analysed so labs could detect it in urine. No human trials of its effects were found.
How it works: It is described as a prohormone that converts to 1-testosterone and related androgens, which act on the androgen receptor.
Risks and caveats: No safety data from human trials exist. Authorities and anti-doping agencies consider such designer androgens related to anabolic steroids.
deepLead:
1-Androsterone, also sold as 1-Andro or 1-DHEA, is a synthetic oral androgen sold online as a "dietary supplement" for muscle gain. Chemically it is 3β-hydroxy-5α-androst-1-en-17-one, a positional isomer of the hormone DHEA.
It is described as a prohormone that is converted in the body to 1-testosterone (dihydroboldenone) and related compounds. The compound is documented mainly in analytical chemistry: a 2011 study identified it in a product seized by German criminal investigators and characterised its urinary elimination so it could be detected in doping control.
No human efficacy or safety trials were found. Authorities and anti-doping bodies treat such designer androgens as pharmacologically related to anabolic steroids.

name: Adrenosterone (11-keto-androstenedione)

chain: Less fat stored, more lean mass
angle.text: Sold as '11-OXO' for fat loss and a leaner physique, with the pitch resting on a proposed cortisol-blocking mechanism. It is a natural adrenal steroid, but supplement trials in people are lacking.

summary: An adrenal steroid sold as '11-OXO' for fat loss via cortisol blocking; the pitch rests on a proposed mechanism with no supplement trials.
note: Doping-control methods exist to detect its use.
currentQuick:
Adrenosterone is a natural adrenal steroid that has been sold since about 2007 as a fat-loss and muscle supplement.
The sources reviewed contain no human trial testing it for that purpose.
How it works: It is proposed to inhibit 11β-HSD1, the enzyme that makes cortisol from cortisone, and it is a precursor to 11-ketotestosterone. Its direct androgen activity is described as extremely weak.
Risks and caveats: No supplement safety data from trials were found. Its legal status is not addressed in the sources reviewed, and anti-doping labs have developed ways to detect it.
deepLead:
Adrenosterone, also called 11-ketoandrostenedione, 11-oxoandrostenedione or Reichstein's substance G, is a steroid made in the adrenal glands. Tadeus Reichstein first isolated it from the adrenal cortex in 1936. It has very weak androgenic activity on its own and is an intermediate and prohormone of 11-ketotestosterone.
Since about 2007 it has been sold as a dietary supplement (often under the name 11-OXO) marketed for fat loss and muscle gain. Proponents attribute this to inhibition of 11β-HSD1, the enzyme that converts cortisone to cortisol, which would reduce cortisol activity; Wikipedia presents this as a proposed mechanism.
No human clinical trial of adrenosterone supplements for body composition was found. Published work covers analytical detection for doping control and the role of 11-oxygenated androgens in conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome.

name: Mebolazine (Dymethazine)

angle.text: Mebolazine turned up in gray-market supplements marketed to bodybuilders as an oral steroid for lean mass gains. It is a dimer of methasterone, and the muscle-building use rests on its steroid class and anecdote; no human studies exist.

summary: A withdrawn oral steroid, a dimer of methasterone, that resurfaced in gray-market supplements; no human studies exist.
note: FDA has taken legal action against supplements containing it.
currentQuick:
Mebolazine is an oral anabolic steroid that was once sold as a medicine and later withdrawn. It reappeared from about 2008 in gray-market supplements.
No clinical studies were found.
How it works: It is reportedly a prodrug of methasterone, an androgen receptor agonist.
Risks and caveats: The FDA has acted against makers of supplements containing it, and it is classed with hepatotoxic oral steroids. Human safety data are absent.
deepLead:
Mebolazine, also called dimethazine or dymethazine, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone and an unusual dimer of methasterone, two units joined by an azine group.
Wikipedia reports that it reportedly acts as a prodrug of methasterone and that it was once marketed as the medicines Dostalon and Roxilon but is no longer sold. Since about 2008 it has been found as an unlisted ingredient in some dietary supplements, and the US FDA has taken legal action against manufacturers of such products.
No clinical trials were found. Published research is limited to metabolism studies.

name: Mestanolone

angle.text: Mestanolone is an old oral 17-methyl DHT steroid that bodybuilders have discussed as a strongly androgenic compound for strength and hardness. Its appearance use rests on class effects and anecdote; modern trials are absent.

summary: An old oral 17-methyl DHT steroid: strongly androgenic, weakly anabolic, mostly discontinued; no modern trials.
note: US Schedule III; hepatotoxic like other 17-alkylated steroids.
currentQuick:
Mestanolone is a mid-20th-century oral steroid derived from DHT. It was sold as a medicine but turned out to be mostly androgenic rather than strongly anabolic.
It is largely discontinued, and the literature on it is mostly about detecting it in doping control.
How it works: It activates the androgen receptor directly and cannot convert to estrogen. The 17-methyl group allows oral activity.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include virilisation and liver damage. It is Schedule III in the US and controlled in many other countries.
deepLead:
Mestanolone (methylandrostanolone, 17α-methyldihydrotestosterone) is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid, a 17α-methylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone (DHT). The methyl group makes it active by mouth, unlike DHT itself.
It was first synthesised in 1935, developed by Roussel in the 1950s and marketed by about 1960, for example as 25 mg sublingual tablets (Ermalone). It was later found to be mainly androgenic with weak anabolic effects. It remains available in Japan but is mostly discontinued elsewhere.
It cannot be aromatised to estrogen. Like other 17α-alkylated steroids it is reported to be hepatotoxic, and virilisation is a listed side effect. It is also a metabolite of oxymetholone and has been studied mostly in doping analysis.

name: Stenbolone

angle.text: Stenbolone, a DHT-derived steroid related to drostanolone, is mentioned in bodybuilding circles for lean muscle and a harder look. It is known mostly from metabolism and doping-detection studies; the physique claim is based on anecdote and class effects.

summary: A DHT-derived anabolic steroid whose acetate ester was an old injectable; known today mostly from metabolism studies.
note: Little human data beyond metabolism.
currentQuick:
Stenbolone is a DHT-derived anabolic steroid. Only its acetate ester was ever sold, as an injectable.
The human literature is thin and mostly concerns metabolism and detection.
How it works: It acts as an androgen receptor agonist; the acetate ester serves as a depot prodrug.
Risks and caveats: No clinical safety data were found beyond its classification as an anabolic steroid. Legal status was not documented in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Stenbolone (2-methyl-Δ1-dihydrotestosterone) is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, related to drostanolone and 1-testosterone. Wikipedia states the compound itself was never marketed.
Its 17β-acetate ester, stenbolone acetate, was sold as a depot intramuscular injection under names such as Anatrofin and Stenobolone. A 1969 Mexican paper examined stenbolone acetate's effects on the normal ovary.
Human data are limited to metabolism studies: after a single oral dose of the acetate to a volunteer, researchers identified nine urinary metabolites and detected the parent compound for more than 120 hours. Equine anti-doping work includes it among screened anabolic steroids.

name: Mepitiostane (Thioderon)

chain: Less water and fat, drier muscle look
angle.text: Mepitiostane is an oral prodrug of epitiostanol that bodybuilders discuss as an antiestrogen for a drier, leaner contest look. It is studied only as a breast-cancer and renal-anemia drug in Japan; the physique use rests on anecdote.

summary: Japanese oral prodrug of the antiestrogen steroid epitiostanol, sold as a breast-cancer and renal-anemia drug; no appearance studies exist.
note: Prescription drug in Japan; listed as prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency; virilizing effects reported in women.
currentQuick:
Mepitiostane, sold in Japan as Thioderon, is an oral steroid that the body converts into epitiostanol. It combines antiestrogen activity with weak anabolic and androgenic activity, and it has been marketed as a treatment for breast cancer and for anemia in kidney failure.
It appears in muscle-building discussions because it is an anabolic-androgenic steroid with antiestrogenic action. No published human study has tested it for muscle, fat loss or other appearance outcomes.
How it works: After absorption, mepitiostane is converted to epitiostanol, which binds the estrogen receptor as an antagonist and the androgen receptor as an agonist. Animal studies show the intact molecule is carried in the intestinal lymph, which lets part of the dose bypass first-pass liver metabolism.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia reports a high rate of virilizing effects in women, such as acne, hirsutism and voice changes. It is prescription-only where it is sold, and sports authorities prohibit it; urine tests for its metabolites have been published for doping control.
deepLead:
Mepitiostane (brand name Thioderon) is an orally active synthetic steroid of the dihydrotestosterone group that acts as an antiestrogen and a weak anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a prodrug, meaning it is converted in the body to epitiostanol, the active compound. 
In Japan it has been marketed for breast cancer and for anemia associated with kidney failure.  Published clinical work includes a phase III comparison with medroxyprogesterone acetate in advanced postmenopausal breast cancer, a study in hemodialysis patients with ACE-inhibitor-related anemia, and a case report of a presumed meningioma that regressed during treatment. 
No published human study has examined mepitiostane for bodybuilding or other appearance goals. Interest in it comes from its classification as an anabolic-androgenic steroid and from its listing in anti-doping analytical literature.

name: Epitiostanol

angle.text: Epitiostanol is an injectable antiestrogen steroid that bodybuilders discuss for a drier, harder look and for limiting gynecomastia. It has been studied in breast cancer, while the muscle and appearance angle has no human data.

summary: Injectable Japanese antiestrogen steroid (Thiodrol) used for breast cancer; the muscle-building angle has no human data behind it.
note: Oral epitiostanol is largely destroyed by first-pass metabolism; the oral prodrug is mepitiostane.
currentQuick:
Epitiostanol is a dihydrotestosterone-derived steroid that blocks the estrogen receptor while weakly activating the androgen receptor. It has been used in Japan since 1977 as an anticancer drug for breast cancer.
It shows up in muscle-related lists because it is classed as an anabolic-androgenic steroid. No published trial has tested it for muscle gain or appearance.
How it works: It binds the estrogen receptor as an antagonist and the androgen receptor as an agonist. In premenopausal women it also suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, lowering estrogen. Orally it is broken down extensively in the gut wall and liver, so it has been given by injection; mepitiostane is an oral prodrug.
Risks and caveats: Little safety information is published in the sources available. A related prodrug, mepitiostane, has a high rate of virilizing effects in women. It is a prescription drug in Japan, and the related compound methylepitiostanol has appeared as a designer steroid.
deepLead:
Epitiostanol (brand name Thiodrol) is a synthetic steroid of the dihydrotestosterone group that acts as an antiestrogen and as a comparatively weak anabolic-androgenic steroid. It has been used in Japan as an antineoplastic drug for breast cancer since 1977. 
Its interest to physique communities stems from its classification as an anabolic steroid. No published human study has examined it for muscle gain or other appearance outcomes. Published human work concerns hormone effects in women and breast cancer treatment.

name: Furazabol

angle.text: Furazabol is a Japanese oral steroid close to stanozolol, discussed by bodybuilders for lean mass and strength. It is known in the West largely from doping history; its physique use rests on class effects and anecdote, with no modern trials.

summary: Oral Japanese anabolic steroid, close cousin of stanozolol, best known in the West from the Ben Johnson doping inquiry; no modern human trials.
note: 17α-alkylated steroid with possible liver toxicity; controlled in the US (Schedule III) and Canada (Schedule IV).
currentQuick:
Furazabol is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid marketed in Japan since 1969. Structurally it is nearly identical to stanozolol, with a furazan ring in place of stanozolol's pyrazole ring.
It is rarely discussed outside doping history. No modern human trial of its effect on muscle or appearance was found; the available sources are mostly doping-control and animal studies.
How it works: It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone and acts on the androgen receptor. It is reported to have a relatively high ratio of anabolic to androgenic activity. Rat studies also reported effects on blood fibrinolysis, and it has been described as lipid-lowering.
Risks and caveats: As a 17α-alkylated steroid it may carry a risk of liver toxicity. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States and Schedule IV in Canada, and anabolic steroids are prohibited in sport.
deepLead:
Furazabol is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid that has been marketed in Japan since 1969. It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone and is structurally close to stanozolol, differing in having a furazan ring where stanozolol has a pyrazole ring. 
Wikipedia reports a relatively high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio and describes antihyperlipidemic properties, which the author William Llewellyn regards as a myth.  Published sources on furazabol are largely animal pharmacology and analytical studies for doping control rather than human efficacy trials. 
In North America furazabol became known through the Dubin Inquiry into the 1988 Olympic doping case of sprinter Ben Johnson.

name: Oxabolone cipionate

angle.text: Oxabolone cipionate is an obscure injectable 19-nor steroid once sold in Europe as Steranabol, and collectors of steroid lore mention it for mass gain. Almost nothing is published; the muscle use rests on its drug class.

summary: Obscure injectable 19-nor steroid ester once marketed in Europe as Steranabol; almost nothing is published about it.
note: Very thin literature; one case report links the parent compound to mucosal hyperpigmentation.
currentQuick:
Oxabolone cipionate is a long-acting injectable ester of oxabolone (4-hydroxy-19-nortestosterone), a nandrolone-type anabolic steroid. It was marketed in Europe under the names Steranabol Depo and Steranabol Ritardo.
Very little has been published on it. No clinical or appearance studies were found.
How it works: It is a prodrug of oxabolone, given by intramuscular injection. Published sources do not describe its pharmacology or potency in detail.
Risks and caveats: The only indexed report found is a 1995 dermatology paper on mucosal hyperpigmentation due to oxabolone. Little else is documented.
deepLead:
Oxabolone cipionate (also spelled cypionate) is a synthetic injected anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone (nandrolone) group. It is the C17β cypionate ester and a prodrug of oxabolone, and it carried the developmental code FI-5852. It has been marketed in Europe under the brand names Steranabol Depo and Steranabol Ritardo. 
Published information is sparse. Wikipedia does not describe indications, pharmacokinetics or regulatory status, and the one indexed medical paper is a case report of mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone.

name: Ethylestrenol (Maxibolin)

angle.text: Ethylestrenol is an old oral 19-nor steroid that bodybuilders have used for lean, low-water mass gains. It was studied medically for wasting and anemia; no trials address appearance.

summary: Old oral 19-nor anabolic steroid, now veterinary-only; Wikipedia calls it a very weak muscle-builder and there are no appearance trials.
note: Schedule III in the US; 17α-alkylated, so liver toxicity is possible; may masculinize a female fetus.
currentQuick:
Ethylestrenol is an oral nandrolone-derived anabolic steroid first described in 1959 and approved in the United States in 1964. It was prescribed to promote weight gain, in catabolic states, and for some anemias and bone conditions.
It is no longer used in humans and appears to survive only as a veterinary product in a few countries. Wikipedia describes it as a very weak muscle-builder, which is why it has not been commonly used for physique purposes.
How it works: It is an androgen receptor agonist with strong progestogenic activity and a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio. It is considered a prodrug of norethandrolone, and its receptor affinity is low, about 5 percent of testosterone's according to Wikipedia.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include virilization (acne, hirsutism, voice changes) and possible liver damage as a 17α-alkylated steroid. Pregnancy and prostate cancer are contraindications. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and Schedule IV in Canada.
deepLead:
Ethylestrenol (also ethyloestrenol; brand names Maxibolin and Orabolin) is a synthetic oral androgen and anabolic steroid with progestogenic activity, derived from nandrolone by 17α-alkylation. It was first described in 1959, approved for medical use in 1961, and approved in the United States in 1964. 
Historically it was prescribed to promote weight gain and muscle growth, for catabolic states such as corticosteroid therapy, chronic infection, surgery and trauma, for treatment-refractory anemias, as an adjunct in osteoporosis and for short stature in young people. It is no longer used in humans and appears to be available only for veterinary use in Australia and New Zealand. 
Wikipedia says it has been used to improve physique and performance but is a very weak muscle-builder compared with other anabolic steroids, so it has not been commonly used for that purpose. No trials of it for appearance outcomes were found.

name: Norethandrolone (Nilevar)

angle.text: Norethandrolone, an early oral anabolic steroid from the 1950s, is cited in bodybuilding history as a forerunner of later steroids for mass. A 1959 weight-gain study is the main data point on muscle; appearance trials are absent.

summary: One of the first oral anabolic steroids (1950s); documented cholestasis and liver injury ended most use, and only a 1959 weight-gain study speaks to muscle.
note: Cholestasis and peliosis hepatis reported in treated patients; withdrawn in many countries in the 1980s.
currentQuick:
Norethandrolone, sold as Nilevar, is an oral 19-nortestosterone steroid synthesized by G. D. Searle in 1953 and introduced as an anabolic steroid in 1956. It was the first anabolic steroid marketed with a favorable separation of anabolic from androgenic effects.
It was prescribed for muscle wasting, burns, trauma and some aplastic anemias. Human data on weight gain come from mid-century studies of underweight patients; it has not been studied for appearance in modern trials.
How it works: It is an androgen receptor agonist with strong progestogenic activity. Wikipedia reports that aromatase converts it to the potent estrogen ethylestradiol, and that its anabolic-to-androgenic ratio in rodents is about 1:1 to 1:2.
Risks and caveats: Cholestasis, peliosis hepatis and bile canalicular changes were reported in treated patients in 1959 and 1960 papers. It was withdrawn in many countries in the 1980s over liver concerns, is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US, and is reported to be available today only in France.
deepLead:
Norethandrolone (brand names Nilevar and Pronabol) is a synthetic, orally taken androgen and anabolic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group, a 17α-ethyl derivative of nandrolone. G. D. Searle synthesized it in 1953, initially as a progestin, and introduced it medically as an anabolic steroid in 1956. Wikipedia describes it as the first anabolic steroid marketed with a favorable separation of anabolic and androgenic effects. 
It was used for muscle wasting, severe burns, trauma and certain aplastic anemias, and was studied for male hormonal contraception. It was sold in the US in the late 1950s as Nilevar and discontinued there in the 1960s because of limited sales, and was withdrawn in many countries in the 1980s over concerns about liver damage including cholestatic jaundice. 
Early clinical papers reported cholestasis and peliosis hepatis in treated patients.  Later, a French randomized trial examined low-dose norethandrolone in elderly acute myeloid leukemia.  No modern trials of norethandrolone for appearance have been found.

currentQuick:
Mibolerone is a synthetic androgen that Upjohn sold as Cheque Drops to stop female dogs coming into heat. It is not approved for people.
In bodybuilding circles it is described as an extremely potent oral steroid taken for short-term strength and aggression. Those claims come from community reports; no human studies back them.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor very tightly, and also the progesterone receptor. Its 17-alkyl group makes it active when swallowed. In dogs it suppresses luteinizing hormone release, which blocks ovulation.
Risks and caveats: Animal use is linked to enlarged clitoris, vaginitis and liver changes. Human risks are inferred from other oral steroids, since no human safety data exist. It is controlled in the US, Canada and Brazil and banned in sport.
deepLead:
Mibolerone, also called dimethylnortestosterone (DMNT) and sold under the brand names Cheque Drops and Matenon, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from nandrolone. It was marketed by the Upjohn Company as a veterinary drug whose labeled purpose was to suppress estrus (heat) in adult female dogs . It is not approved for human use.
In laboratory science, mibolerone is used as a high-affinity androgen receptor ligand in studies of prostate and breast cancer cell lines . Outside veterinary and laboratory settings, it is discussed in bodybuilding and strength-sport circles as a very potent oral androgen, and it is a controlled substance in several countries (Schedule III in the United States, Schedule IV in Canada) and prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency .
No published clinical trial has tested mibolerone in humans for muscle gain, appearance or any other purpose. Claims about its effects on people come from community reports and from extrapolation of its receptor pharmacology.
